gaps: No parent mode at all, and the assistant's context builder (prompts.dart, guide_search.dart) is built for the account owner's own record; it would answer about the daughter as if the parent were her if the parent used the same phone.

Must NOT reveal from her daughter's record: any log, flow, symptom or mood term, cycle dates or predictions, notes, screener answers, what she read or asked, whether she has logged at all, why sharing changed.
No under-18 rule in the assistant (MR-48 age gate exists for the app but not in assistant prompts).
Assistant must keep the same on-device rule for minors: nothing about a minor goes to the cloud model; the redaction.dart list does not cover 'my daughter' phrases.
No parent-facing guides confirmed in the guide index for 'how to talk about periods'.

name: Partner mode (supporting a woman through trying, pregnancy or postpartum)
aiJobs: Education: plain, short guides for a partner on supporting someone who is trying, pregnant or recovering, including his own wellbeing (partners can get postnatal depression too).
Support cues: a calm daily 'how can I help' prompt that does not reveal cycle phase, test results or symptoms.
Visit prep: shared appointment lists and a question list for him, nothing from her log unless she shared it.
Safety: if he describes danger signs about her (bleeding, severe headache), show the general warning card and 'call emergency services', without any record access.
covered: Product has no accounts and keeps her record on her phone, so there is no remote way for him to see anything.
safety.dart danger-sign rules can run on text he types without any record.
gaps: No partner mode exists; the assistant has no concept of whose record is open, so if he uses her phone he would see her Ask history and log.

Must NOT reveal from her record: cycle day or phase, fertile window, ovulation tests, intercourse log, pregnancy test results (until she announces), symptoms, moods, notes, screener answers, anything she asked the assistant, or whether she has logged.
No coercion-aware rule: assistant should never help someone obtain another person's health data or advise on pressuring conception (ACOG reproductive coercion).
Elevated terms (libido, intercourse, painDuringSex, vaginalDryness) already hide on shared screens, but assistant answers and visit summaries could still echo them; needs a shared-screen guard.
No degendered copy for same-sex or single-parent households.
